items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 70:1
items.html: It is known that the ten Sefirot of the hairs were also corrected in the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK of Tzelem, in which the MEM in them was refined and ascended to be the hairs of the head, and the LAMED-TZADIK in them became the hairs of the beard. Hence the aspect of the LAMED-TZADIK of the hairs is considered dregs and waste of the hairs of the head, for they are only the aspect of the MEM of Tzelem — and therefore they attached to the Galgalta, which is also the aspect of MEM, as is known. Now, these dregs of the hairs of the head are considered harsh judgments, for the hairs of the beard are harsh judgments, as is known. And after the hairs of the beard were also refined and joined in their place, there remain the dregs left after them, which are the aspect of complete waste, no longer fit for anything, for all the holiness was already refined from them — as above, Page 313, Item 41, that after all the holiness is refined from them, they are discerned as shells in which there is no benefit at all. See there. (Page 376, Item 171).
